Mapping out the pattern: (17,1)=1, (15,3)=2, and (13,5)=4 sit on the diagonal itself, while (17,3)/(15,1)=3 and (13,7)/(11,5)=8 form symmetric off-diagonal pairs — matching the example's structure where diagonal values pair with branching values that get extended into square rings.

So the pattern is: each branch cell's distance from its nearest edge determines the inset of the square it generates. Applying this to the given pairs: pair 3 at (17,3)/(15,1) sits at inset 1 from the edge, giving a square at rows/cols 1 and 17; pair 8 at (13,7)/(11,5) sits at inset 5, giving a square at rows/cols 5 and 13.

Diagonal cells also mark corners of these inset squares — the value-1 diagonal cell marks corners of the inset-1 square, value-2 marks corners of an inset-3 square (points only, no drawn square), and value-4 marks corners of the inset-5 square, which coincides with the square generated by branch pair 8.

Working through the dotted spacing (every 2 positions along rows/cols 1 and 17), corners get value 1 and remaining dotted points get value 3, matching the example pattern. Now I'm assembling the full 19x19 grid, filling in coordinates according to these rules.

Checking the (15,3)=2 and (17,3)=3 values confirm the pattern holds, so I'm building out each row explicitly now, placing the symmetric values at their correct column positions row by row.
